newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysian rubber closes down on weak sentiment.
newsitem.headline: Malaysian rubber closes down on weak sentiment.

text.p: Malaysian rubber prices ended Friday lower in tandem with weaker Tokyo futures prices and the absence of consumer demand, traders said.
"It was a quiet day through...there was no news of even inquiries," said a dealer as he packed up for the week.
Another trader said the recent weakness of Thai rubber prices was also a factor for the depressed local market.
"All overseas buyers seem sidelined at the moment," said a trader. Japanese rubber futures prices are expected to keep falling due to poor-quality rubber coming to market, traders there said.
At the close, the Malaysian Rubber Exchange and Licensing Board quoted July RSS1 buyer at 263.50 cents ($1.04) a kg, down four cents from Friday. July SMR20 buyer fell a cent to 245.50.
Trading houses offered the SMR 20 at 244, SMR 10 at 245, SMR CV at 312 cents, SMR L at 291 cents, and latex at 213 cents.
Traders said prices were expected to stay soft in the week ahead and could fall between three and five cents a grade.
The INRO five-day average was 201.58 Malaysian/Singapore cents a kg on June 26 from 203.6 on June 25. The daily indicator was at 197.95 against 200.04.
